newsitem.title: UK: Granada's Robinson sees one owner for ITV.
newsitem.headline: Granada's Robinson sees one owner for ITV.

text.p: Granada chairman Gerry Robinson said on Wednesday he expected the UK's ITV commercial television network ultimately to be owned by one big media player.
"I think it is the ultimate future," he said when asked at a news conference about the possibility of all 15 regional licensees being owned by one group.
"If ITV were started now it would look a ludicrous and costly structure to compete with Sky, Channel 4 and Channel 5," Robinson said.
"It could be in 10-15 years but it would be absolutely logical (to have one owner)," he added.
ITV is in the process of consolidation after the UK last year lifted a two-licence cap on ownership and replaced it with a maximum of 15 percent of the total TV audience.
Granada, Carlton and United News & Media are emerging as the key players in England and Wales while Scottish Media is building up its interests north of the border.
Granada chief executive Charles Allen said he expected the Independent Television Commission (ITC) to seek to smooth out huge differences in what different regional operators pay for their licences.

The licences run for 10 years from 1993 but companies can seek an early renewal from 1999. The ITC is expected to publish shortly a document outlining how it plans to handle applications for early renewal.
"A system which has some companies paying 2,000 pounds per year and others almost 50 million pounds clearly did not get it right," Allen said. "Clearly we think there would be a balancing out."
Companies made a cash bid as part of their licence application in 1991. Those that did not expect to face competition for their licence offered only a nominal sum.
Yorkshire-Tyne Tees Television, with which Granada is in preliminary offer talks, has long campaigned for a cut in what it pays for its two licences. Its licence fees were 66 million stg last year.
Allen said the licence fee issue was bound up with the elimination of the Channel 4 funding formula, which has benefited ITV companies in recent years.

Under the formula, Channel 4 must hand over a chunk of its advertising revenue to the ITV companies when its revenue tops 14 percent of terrestrial TV advertising and sponsorship income. ITV must support Channel 4 if its revenue falls below that level.
The ITV companies made 87 million stg from the arrangement last year.
National Heritage Secretary Chris Smith is taking soundings from broadcasters on the formula. It is expected to be phased out but the details and timetable for its removal are still to be settled.
